text:
Maya: quick update from the batcher sweep this morning — ran a multi-card experiment sweeping max_tokens_per_batch across A10/T4/L4/A100/H100. found some interesting kernel-fit regressions on L4 when slice gating enabled. attaching brief profiler snippets and numbers below.

Sam: thanks — can you drop the raw numbers? curious about throughput/latency tradeoffs.

Maya: sure. highlights:
- A10: stable with softcap at 80k tokens/batch for our default seq dist, slight CPU overhead when KV prefetching enabled.
- T4: best at ~40k tokens/batch; above that we start seeing kernel fallback to slower matmul path.
- L4: problematic past ~50k — kernel selector prefers fallback kernel causing 20–30% p99 latency regression when slice-gating = on.
- A100: tolerant up to 160k, but KV frag increases memory churn if we pack too aggressively.
- H100: best raw throughput, recommended 200k softcap but watch for tail latency with mixed packing.

Liam: interesting — do we have kernel selection logs? looks like selector version v2.3.1 was used?

Maya: yes, selector v2.3.1. excerpt from kernel-decider log: ```kernel_decision { model: "llama-13b" seq_len:512 batch_tokens:56000 device: "L4" selector_version: "v2.3.1" chosen: "fallback_matmul" reason: "kv-frag > 0.7 and quantized_path_unavailable" }```

Aditya: that explains it. v2.3.1 has a conservative threshold for L4's fused attention kernel when KV fragmentation > 0.6. we tuned that down in the prototype branch but didn't A/B it at scale.

Sam: did you try the prototype thresholds? any perf numbers?

Maya: yes — prototype threshold lowered KV_frag threshold from 0.6 -> 0.75 (i.e., more permissive), and we saw L4 p99 improve ~18% at 60k tokens/batch, but memory tail events increased slightly. raw microprofile snippet: ```profile: { device: L4, batch_tokens: 60000, p50: 32ms, p95: 120ms, p99: 360ms, mem_peak: 10.2GB, kv_frag: 0.68, chosen_kernel: fused_attn_v2 }```

Liam: are those runs with slice-gating on?

Maya: yes slice-gating = true for those. turns out gating causes more variable sequence packing which increases KV frag in unpredictable ways.

Aditya: proposal: introduce a soft-slice cap — when predicted kv_frag > 0.7, prefer smaller max_tokens cap for that slice class. this keeps fused kernel but avoids mem thrash. config sketch: ```batcher.soft_slice_cap = true; slice.kv_frag_threshold = 0.7; slice.max_tokens_scale = 0.85;```

Sam: sounds reasonable. can we autosample workloads to learn per-model per-device softcap? would need signal from production traces (seq dist + kv_frag).

Maya: I ran a lightweight sampler overnight on prod traffic (shadow mode) and produced per-model suggestions: A10: 0.8*baseline, T4: 0.9, L4: 0.75, A100: 1.0, H100: 1.1. attaching CSV to the ticket.

deploy-bot: deployment started for batcher-experiments/soft-slice-cap v0.1 -> staging (canary 10% traffic).

Sam: thanks. next steps:
1) Aditya to push an experimental gate that tunes kv_frag threshold per-device (PR please).
2) Maya to open an eval comparing selector v2.3.1 vs prototype across our model matrix (llama-7b/13b/70b).
3) Liam to add a perf regression alert rule for fallback kernel occurrences > 5% per minute on L4.

Aditya: I can do the PR today. will include toggle flags and telemetry counters (KV_frag, kernel_chosen, mem_peak).

Maya: I'll own the eval and baseline CSV upload. expect results by EOD tomorrow.

Liam: if we see mem_peak increase > 5% on A100/H100, we should auto-backoff packing aggressiveness. I'll draft the alert.

Sam: Great. one more ask — can we add a small logging field indicating "slice_gating=on/off" to the kernel_decision log to make debugging easier?

Aditya: yes will add that to the PR.

Maya: thanks team :thumbsup: will post the staging canary link and CSV once available.
